customManagers.description: wasm-bindgen-cli is installed by `cargo install` in workflow files, which no built-in manager reads. Without this, Renovate bumps the crate pin and leaves the CLI behind.

packageRules.description: Tag-tracking deps (non-semver refs, e.g. dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable, or a Dockerfile FROM pinned to a floating tag + digest like rust:1.98.0-bookworm) only get digest updates, which have no release timestamp, so the age gate would block them forever. Same for `pin`/`pinDigest`: pinning rewrites a range or tag to what is already in use (`0.25.1` -> `=0.25.1`), so there is no new release to age, and Renovate does not support minimumReleaseAge for pin updates. Left gated, the whole `pin dependencies` PR sits `pending` forever
Patch updates are low-review-effort; land them as one PR

Pinned, not bumped: under `bump` the manifest gets a caret range, and `cargo update` resolves past the version Renovate picked once `minimumReleaseAge` holds a newer release back (jsonschema 0.58.3 vs 0.58.5, PR #597). `=x.y.z` leaves cargo no room to resolve anything else. Lockfile maintenance is disabled (top of file) for the same reason: it refreshes every transitive crate to the newest in-range release with no age check, and a whole-lockfile refresh has no release timestamp for the gate to measure. With direct deps pinned and no scheduled refresh, Cargo.lock only changes when a gated bump forces it; transitive security fixes come from `cargo audit` in ci.yml.

optative-script pins an rquickjs major, and tauler uses rquickjs types directly at the UI-component registration boundary (src/ui/registry.rs, src/jsx.rs). Two rquickjs versions in the graph make `Ctx`/`Error` fail to unify, so a lone bump of any one of these never compiles. Pinned, not bumped: a caret range lets `cargo update` resolve past the version Renovate picked, which is how the two copies get in.
tauler and optative are deeply intertwined and often developed together, so the release-age delay on optative crates is counter-productive. rquickjs stays gated: it is third-party.

takumi re-exports takumi-core types; a lone bump of either puts two takumi-core versions in the graph and the ImageSource/ImageBuffer types stop unifying. Pinned for the same reason as the quickjs group — under `bump`, `minimumReleaseAge` held takumi at 2.7.3 while the lockfile update resolved 2.9.2, and the two takumi-core versions that pulled in did not compile.

The wasm-bindgen CLI refuses to process a module built against a different version of the crate, so the crate pins (tauler-core, tauler-web) and the CLI installs in workflows are one version in several places. Pinned and grouped so they move together; a lone crate bump also breaks `cargo publish` of dependents until the next tauler-core release (#605).
Starlight and its themes/integrations peer-depend on the Astro major.
Action digest bumps are independent and noisy; one PR is enough.

docs-ci.yaml pins its job container to the same mcr.microsoft.com/playwright image tag docs/scripts/update-snapshots.sh derives from @playwright/test — two copies of one version (ADR 0031). Overrides the generic github-actions grouping above so this doesn't drift out of sync inside a batch of unrelated action bumps.

TypeScript 7's native compiler doesn't expose the programmatic API @astrojs/language-server's `astro check` needs yet (https://github.com/withastro/roadmap/discussions/1321). A major bump landed anyway and broke Docs CI outright, not just with new lint findings — block it until Astro's tooling catches up.
